title: Using Macroeconomic Forecasts to Improve Mean Reverting Trading Strategies

extraction.methodology_summary: The strategy implements a multiple pairs trading framework on major currency pairs using cointegration tested via the Johansen procedure. A mean reversion trading signal is generated using z-scores of the cointegrated portfolio spreads with entry and exit thresholds. To improve performance, a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifies the monthly directional movement of macroeconomic variables (S&P 500, Federal Funds Rate, and 10-Year Treasury Yield), and the resulting signals are combined with the mean-reverting signal using weights optimized via Sequential Least-Squares Programming (SLSQP) to maximize APR.
extraction.universe: Major currency pairs retrieved through Yahoo Finance

performance_metrics.context: Mean reversion strategy considering only the mean reverting signal
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: If only the mean reverting signal was considered, an APR of 4.084% was yielded.

performance_metrics.context: Mean reversion strategy after optimization, giving non-zero weight to macroeconomic indicators
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: After optimization, giving non-zero weight to the macroeconomic indicators was found to be ideal, with a increased APR of 4.112% obtained.

key_findings: Macroeconomic indicators combined with technical mean reversion signals improve trading strategy performance.
Support Vector Machines can forecast the directional movement of macroeconomic indicators with a classification accuracy of 70%.
Incorporating macroeconomic forecasts prevents excessive transitioning between long and short positions during major macroeconomic events such as the 2008-2009 recession.
limitations: The lessening in the APR is due to the transaction costs factored in.
